messages.allocation.advisor: Review how this course is assigned across requirements.
messages.allocation.financePetition: You may petition to count BUSN 323 as an Economics elective. This plan does not count it yet. Talk with your advisor about the petition.
messages.allocation.move: This move must preserve the approved requirement assignment.

display.adjunct: An additional Economics elective may be possible in Fall or Winter, but the course, funding, and instructor are not confirmed. Ask your advisor before relying on it.
display.capstone: Senior capstone · Winter. Final year preferred.
display.caveat: A past schedule does not guarantee a course will be offered again.
display.finance: Prefer BUSN 323 when it fits. Future BUSN 323 offerings need confirmation; future ECO 321 adjunct staffing is uncertain.
display.future: For terms without a published schedule, this plan assumes no more than one Economics elective per term. Actual offerings may differ.
display.hs: Either ECO 113 or ECO 114 counts as one of the two HS courses. The other must be from a different discipline.
display.intermediate: In past schedules, ECO 213 and ECO 214 were offered in different Fall or Winter terms. Their order changed from year to year. A published schedule may differ.
display.prerequisiteCompletion: Complete planned prerequisites before their dependent courses.
display.seatConfirmation: Confirm seat availability before registration; the published schedule is not current seat confirmation.

authorityHierarchy: An active authoritative exact schedule controls its matching year and term.
Department-confirmed Economics policy controls only its documented departmental boundary.
Applicable catalog or approved catalog-derived records control formal requirements and prerequisites.
College-wide rules outrank departmental exceptions unless override authority is explicit.
Department-approved recurring policies may guide unpublished years.
Historical observations may support preliminary projections but are not hard rules by repetition alone.
Unpublished schedules are never called verified.
A later exact schedule overrides a projection for that exact year.
Expired or superseded records cannot remain active.
Unresolved conflict yields review or TBC, not an invented allow or block.
Precedence uses authority, boundary, scope, dates, and supersession, never file order or most-restrictive-wins.

sources.statement: For the existing ECO 461 concurrency exception, exactly one of ECO 213 or ECO 214 must be successfully completed before the target ECO 461 term. Eligible completed and accepted-transfer evidence, a current in-progress course finishing before the target term, and an earlier generated-term course may count. Same-term or later courses and uncertain or unaccepted history, equivalency, substitution, waiver, or prerequisite evidence do not count. Earlier in-progress or planned completion remains conditional on success. This clarifies the existing 2026-08-01 department-confirmed exception and creates no new exception or alternate planning mode.

unresolved.question: What evidence establishes historical prerequisite satisfaction for an already completed or transferred advanced course?
unresolved.requiredDisposition: Preserve completed history and emit REVIEW_REQUIRED; do not infer or erase facts.

unresolved.question: Which documented courses or equivalencies satisfy the MAT 121 equivalent language for ECO 335?
unresolved.requiredDisposition: Accept explicit MAT 121; review claimed equivalents.

unresolved.question: What governed decision applies when a section is FULL?
unresolved.requiredDisposition: Return REVIEW_REQUIRED; never silently treat FULL as OPEN or CLOSED.

unresolved.question: What are the original schedule release date, retrieval time, availability-as-of time, and human verification time?
unresolved.requiredDisposition: Preserve null timestamps and do not invent them.

unresolved.question: How does a waiver, substitution, or equivalency apply separately to prerequisites and major requirements?
unresolved.requiredDisposition: Require documented authority and scope for each use.
